name: release-agent-flow
body: The optional, per-repo release path: a repo may have the `agent-builder` scaffold a generated `release-agent` — a hidden subagent that is the ONLY generated agent granted `git push`/`git tag` (as `ask`, so every push/tag command prompts for explicit human approval) plus write access to the repo's release artefacts (version files, formulae, changelog, …) — which the `codebase-navigator` tasks ONLY after capturing explicit user consent. The flow exists to make a repo's release repeatable by an agent while keeping the human gate explicit: approval surfaces both at dispatch (the navigator's consent) and per command (the `ask` grant). Every other generated agent gets no push/tag grant at all (denied by deny-by-default). The release-agent is the deliberate carve-out from the recurring "push/tag remain human-approved acts" law. The binary never pushes or tags (git2 only, `default-features = false`; the git CLI is never shelled out to) and `scripts/release.sh` never pushes — the agent may run the script and then push/tag itself.
